name: SEOmedSEB Smart Search for WooCommerce
author: SEOmedSEB

sections.description:
SEOmedSEB Smart Search for WooCommerce is a fast, self-hosted AJAX search plugin for WooCommerce stores, focused on two things:

  1. Deep, code-free design customization. The Design tab exposes colors, typography, spacing, border radius, and several built-in style presets (minimal, command palette, glassmorphism, sharp, rounded) as CSS variables, with a live preview.
  2. A relevance engine with typo tolerance built in. Search runs against a dedicated, optimized index table (not the slow default WordPress search), with fuzzy/SOUNDEX fallback matching so misspelled searches still find the right product.

Every feature in this plugin — including the search engine, the full Design tab, analytics, and the indexer — is free. There is no “Pro” upsell built into this version.

Key features

  • Custom, optimized search index (own DB table, not wp_posts LIKE queries)
  • AJAX autocomplete with grouped results: products, categories, tags, posts, pages
  • Product detail panel on hover — add to cart without leaving the search results
  • Typo-tolerant search (fuzzy/SOUNDEX fallback + “did you mean” suggestions)
  • Synonyms, and exclude/include filter rules by category, tag, or product
  • Full search-scope control (description, short description, SKU, attributes, categories, tags, custom fields)
  • Deep design customization: colors, typography, spacing, radius, style presets, dark mode
  • Animated (“typewriter”) placeholder with a configurable phrase list and speed
  • ⌘K / Ctrl+K global search shortcut
  • Mobile overlay mode with configurable breakpoint
  • Client-side “recent searches” history
  • Search analytics: critical (zero-result) search phrases report + dashboard widget
  • Scheduled + on-demand index rebuilding, with live progress in the admin

Adding the search bar to your theme

  1. Shortcode: [smart_search_bar]
  2. Widget: Appearance → Widgets → “Smart Search bar”
  3. PHP: <?php echo do_shortcode( '[smart_search_bar]' ); ?>
sections.installation:
1. Upload the seomedseb-smart-search folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin. WooCommerce must already be installed and active.
  3. The plugin will automatically build its search index in the background. Check progress under WooCommerce → Smart Search → Indexer.
  4. Add [smart_search_bar] wherever you want the search bar to appear, or use the widget.
sections.faq:
Does this require WooCommerce?

Yes, WooCommerce must be installed and active.

Is this really free?

Yes. Every feature described above is included at no cost. A future paid tier may exist someday, but it is a separate, later decision and does not affect this version.

Does it work with variable products?

Yes, and you choose how. Under Search config → Product variations you can show only the parent product (variation SKUs still match it), give each variation its own result row with its own price, stock and image, or list the matching variations underneath their parent.
sections.changelog:
0.19.15

  • Fixed: browsers that offer speech recognition without a working speech service behind it (Samsung Internet, Instagram/Facebook in-app browsers, some Android WebViews) left the microphone blinking or did nothing. The failure is now detected, the shopper is told, and the microphone button is hidden for the rest of the visit.

0.19.14

  • Fixed: voice search did nothing on iPhone/iPad Safari, which often never finishes a recognition result. The words now appear in the field while you speak, and the search runs after a short pause.
  • Added: when the microphone is blocked or speech recognition is switched off on the device, the search field says so instead of silently doing nothing (text editable under Texts).

0.19.13

  • Fixed: when a search word opens a page and that page also matched by title, it was listed twice.

0.19.12

  • Fixed: page search matched words inside other words, so “om os” listed pages containing “hos”. Every search word must now start a word in the page title.

0.19.11

  • Improved: with “Show pages” switched on, pages are found by their title (“prisgaranti”, “om oss”, “köpvillkor”) and listed above the products. Page content is no longer searched, so the terms page doesn’t turn up for every search, and the checkout page and password-protected pages are left out.
  • Fixed: a search that only matched a page, post or category showed “No results found” instead of the match, and could be “corrected” into an unrelated product.
  • Fixed: with the details panel switched off, the results list now uses the full width instead of leaving an empty column.

0.19.10

  • Fixed: the “Showing results for” note and the “+N more” SKU text could not be changed under Texts, so they stayed in English on sites without a translation. Both are now editable there.

0.19.9

  • Improved: products with exactly the same score are now ordered by sales and then newest first, so the order is stable instead of changing after every index rebuild.

0.19.8

  • Fixed: a word that sounds like a brand now wins over a different word that is merely two letters off (“sabata” finds Savotta instead of “Strata”).

0.19.7

  • Fixed: spelling correction no longer swaps a word for an unrelated one that only shares its ending (a brand the shop doesn’t carry, like “helikon”, was “corrected” to “silikon”). Two-letter corrections now need the same first letter.

0.19.6

  • Fixed: when the Indexing page was open during a rebuild, the page and WP-Cron could both advance the rebuild and skip whole batches of products, which the final clean-up then removed from the index (they disappeared from search until the next full rebuild). Each batch now runs exactly once, in order, and the clean-up only runs when (nearly) the whole catalogue was refreshed.
  • Fixed: when a misspelling was corrected, the “Showing results for …” note took a cell of the two-column results layout, squeezing the product list into a small box and moving the details panel to the left.
  • Improved: spelling correction also matches words that sound alike, which is how voice search and people typing what they hear spell brand names (“sabata” → Savotta, “paksafe” → Pacsafe, “milltek” → Mil-Tec, “helicon” → Helikon-Tex).
  • Added: a new “Extra features” tab. Every feature in it is off until you switch it on, so updating changes nothing on its own:
  • Popular searches shown when the search field is opened empty — picked automatically from Search Analytics, or your own list.
  • Recently viewed products shown when the search field is opened empty (remembered in the visitor’s browser only).
  • Search words that open a page: e.g. “shipping” or “returns” go straight to that page, from the dropdown and on Enter.
  • A weekly e-mail listing the searches that found nothing, with a “send now” button.
  • Voice search: a microphone button, in browsers with built-in speech recognition.
  • Units: “30 liter”, “30 l” and “30L” (and mm, cm, ml, kg, g) are treated as the same.
  • Fixed: on phones, the full-screen search overlay closed again the instant the field was tapped (the overlay moves the bar up, and the tap then landed on the backdrop), so search history never stayed visible on mobile. It now stays open.

Earlier versions

The full changelog back to the 0.1.0 initial release (0.18.33 through 0.1.0) is kept in changelog-full.txt in the plugin’s own folder, and in the version history on this plugin’s SVN repository — trimmed here so this section stays under WordPress.org’s 5000-character display limit for the Changelog tab.
